source.title: Learning Stages: Phenomenon, Root Cause, Mechanism Hypothesis, and Implications
source.authors: Kai-Chao You; Mingsheng Long; Michael I. Jordan; Jian-Min Wang

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendix; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how learning-rate decay affects training and held-out performance with different optimizers and on a constructed noisy-data task, using measures outside the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper studies learning-rate decay, an unlisted training condition. Its ImageNet transferability results concern transfer across datasets and are excluded because out-of-distribution transfer is separate. Figure-only accuracy values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study tests explanations of learning-rate decay, but none of V1–V8. Its GD and SGD experiments vary schedules within each optimizer rather than compare batch sizes under a fixed epoch budget. Noise fitting on PS10 does not test random-label versus natural-label generalization or removal of memorized examples.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors argue that conventional optimization explanations are insufficient, propose that decay enables complex-pattern learning while an initially large rate suppresses noise memorization, and report direct support on PS10 plus indirect support from transferability experiments on real datasets.
record.recipe_differences: Studies learning-rate decay and pattern complexity, rather than the interventions or measures in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with learning-rate schedule and optimizer: SGD shows a post-decay performance boost, while Gradient Descent shows negligible benefit from decay timing.

fits_no_version.finding: Decay timing provides negligible benefit under full-batch GD, while SGD shows a noticeable post-decay performance improvement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate decay affects WideResNet CIFAR-10 training differently under GD and SGD in the tested schedules.

fits_no_version.finding: On PS10 with 10% noise, an initially large learning rate with decay improves complex-pattern accuracy and suppresses noise fitting relative to a constant small rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An initially large learning rate can suppress noise memorization and improve complex-pattern learning on PS10.

fits_no_version.finding: AutoDecay uses 81 rather than 90 epochs, with top-1 accuracy 75.91% versus 75.80% and top-5 accuracy 92.81% versus 92.76%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AutoDecay preserves reported ResNet-50 ImageNet accuracy while reducing training epochs by 10%.

record.problems: Several key accuracy comparisons are figure-only, without precise values or uncertainty estimates. The constructed PS10 task is synthetic; the paper says real-world pattern complexity is intractable.
record.rows_left_out: ImageNet-to-target-dataset transferability results in Figure 11 and Table 2 were left out because they measure transfer across datasets, which the claim explicitly treats separately. Figure 9 pattern-accuracy comparisons are not extracted because this output focuses on results bearing on held-out generalization or the reported noisy-data memorization mechanism; the text gives no held-out designation for those pattern accuracies.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect random-label fitting and natural-label held-out generalization, including chance held-out performance for random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification generalization and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and whether recipe adaptations remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, or augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance ranking generalization gaps relative to other measures. Hessian eigenvalues alone do not test this.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No listed version receives a verdict. The transferability results and Hessian analysis also measure constructs outside V1–V8. States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, without disputing the reported schedule effects.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting random labels with generalization on natural labels.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected architectures.
Studies SGD and gradient descent, not adaptive optimizers or their comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-measure comparison.

rows.subject: WideResNet
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 with Gradient Descent; learning-rate decay timing varied, including no decay.
rows.note: Authors state final performances are almost the same regardless of when the learning rate is decayed.
rows.check: The reported negligible effect concerns decay timing under full-batch GD, not any listed version. The original absent state describes an unlisted effect.

rows.subject: WideResNet
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 with SGD; learning-rate decay timing varied, including no decay.
rows.note: Authors report a noticeable performance difference before and after decay and say the no-decay run plateaus without reaching post-decay performance.
rows.check: The post-decay test-accuracy improvement concerns learning-rate schedules, not a listed version. Comparison with R1 does not establish V5: the GD and SGD figures use different epoch budgets.

rows.subject: WideResNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared learning-rate decay with constant learning rates on PS10 with 10% noisy data.
rows.note: Separate simple-pattern accuracy plot; no precise values or textual comparison stated.
rows.check: Simple-pattern accuracy under different learning-rate schedules measures no listed version; the text also does not establish that this is held-out accuracy.

rows.subject: WideResNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared learning-rate decay with constant learning rates on PS10 with 10% noisy data.
rows.note: Authors state an initially large learning rate helps accuracy on complex patterns.
rows.check: Complex-pattern accuracy under different schedules measures no listed version. It does not supply V1's random-label and natural-label comparison.

rows.subject: WideResNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared learning-rate decay with constant learning rates on PS10 with 10% noisy data.
rows.note: Authors interpret larger noise-data accuracy as undesirable overfitting and state that an initially large learning rate suppresses fitting noisy data.
rows.check: Accuracy on injected noise measures noise fitting, not V1's paired generalization comparison or V8's example-removal intervention.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Replaced StepDecay with AutoDecay for ImageNet training.
rows.note: Authors report AutoDecay shortened training time by 10% without hurting performance; this row records the stated top-1 values.
rows.check: This is performance of the authors' AutoDecay method against StepDecay and should be excluded from claim-evidence rows. Values are correct percentages; the displayed result is captioned Figure 14, although the prose calls it Table 14.

rows.operation_detail: Replaced StepDecay with AutoDecay for ImageNet training.
rows.note: Authors report AutoDecay shortened training time by 10% without hurting performance; this row records the stated top-5 values.
